lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hey Darnell, Luis here. How's your Wednesday going?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi Luis. Give me one second... okay, I'm here.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How's your body feeling this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good. Busy, but good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's great to hear.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: The research is very clear, you have to eat earlier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. We had a birthday party, there was so much food.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Lots of celebrations this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I've always eaten late, that's how we do it at home.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, the hunger at night makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Being around for my family is why I'm doing this. Some days are better than others.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Work has been crazy, I'm doing overtime.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Work took over this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I really want to feel like myself again. I wrote it on the calendar.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My family eats late, like at 9, and I'm not going to eat alone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Dinner's late at your house.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My sugar was better the weeks I ate earlier. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe finish eating by 7:30 on 5 nights?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Darnell. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

flags.reason: Cites research and says he 'has to' eat earlier, pushing advice without permission amid ambivalence.
'You have to make this a priority' directs rather than explores; he had just voiced his own reasons (family).

score.summary: Darnell voiced real change talk (family, feeling better, a fridge reminder, and a concrete 7:30 goal), and the coach did well with complex reflections and let him set the goal. However, two persuading lines ('The research is very clear,' 'You have to make this a priority') pushed against his ambivalence, and the session did not review last goal or summarize.
strengths: Line 17 and line 31: complex reflections that capture ambivalence and his wish to make it fit real life.
Line 33: open question let Darnell choose a doable goal himself.
Line 23 and line 29: reflections that link his change to family and momentum, strengthening change talk.
Line 35: clear next-contact plan with a midweek text and a two-week follow-up.
coaching_tips: Replace 'The research is very clear, you have to eat earlier' (line 8) with an ask-permission lead, e.g., 'Would it be okay if I shared some information about meal timing?'
Avoid 'You have to make this a priority' (line 19); reflect his stated reason instead, e.g., 'Being there for your family is what matters most to you.'
Open the next session by reviewing his last goal and asking how the fridge reminder worked.
Before closing, summarize his plan and ask what might get in the way on the late family dinners (line 26).
